    5-4-3-2-1 Grounding

    My Next Right Step

    You’re not alone in this moment

    A hard moment is not a failure — and you don’t have to carry it by yourself. Reach out right now, in whichever way feels possible:

    Call 988 Text 988

    The 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline — free, confidential, 24/7, anywhere in the U.S.

    Call SAMHSA: 1-800-662-4357

    SAMHSA’s National Helpline — free, confidential treatment referrals and support, 24/7.

    Grounding & prayer

    A prayer for this moment: Lord, I can’t carry this moment alone, and I don’t have to. You are my refuge and my strength, always ready to help. Slow my breathing, steady my heart, and walk me to the next right step. Amen.

    Before you stop drinking

    Alcohol withdrawal can be dangerous. If you drink heavily, don’t try to stop suddenly on your own — talk to a doctor first, or call SAMHSA at 1-800-662-4357 and ask what to do. Getting medical help to stop is not weakness; it’s wisdom.

    Gratitude Journal

    Private, for your eyes only. On hard days, this list is evidence: proof that even in the middle of the rebuilding, there is something to thank God for. Your entries are saved on this device, so they will be here when you come back.

    Nothing here yet. Your first entry can be as small as a cup of coffee, a phone call, or waking up sober this morning.

    My Next Right Step

    Recovery is built one small, honest step at a time. Don't write the whole staircase — just the next step: the call to make, the meeting to attend, the thing to hand to God today.

    No steps yet. Add the one thing in front of you today — that's enough.

    THE FOUNDER'S JOURNEY

    One day at a time

    Steven Gregory — counting from August 20, 2026 (Day 0).

    Why this app exists

    My name is Steven Gregory. After 34 years of struggling with alcohol — rehabs, jail, losing everything I owned more than once, including my career — I started this recovery journey on August 20, 2026. I am living it the only way it can be lived: one day at a time.

    My Christian faith is the ground I stand on. I pray every day, and prayer is what keeps me holding on. When I say God restores, I mean it the way Joel 2:25 says it — He gives back what was lost.

    I built My Recovery Journey, and now this app, for the person who feels alone in recovery tonight. You are not alone. These are the same tools I use every day: count the days, read the reflection, write the gratitude, take the next right step.

    “One Day at a Time. One Step Toward a New Life.”

        Install My Recovery Journey

        This is your icon — the gold path through the evergreens to the sunrise. Once installed, it sits on your home screen and opens full-screen, just like an app from the store.

        On iPhone — Safari

        1. Open this page in Safari on your iPhone (if you're in another app's browser, tap its menu and choose “Open in Safari”).
        2. Tap the Share button — the square with an arrow pointing up ↑ — at the bottom of Safari.
        3. Scroll down the list and tap “Add to Home Screen.”
        4. Check the name reads My Recovery Journey, then tap Add in the top corner.
        5. Find the gold-path icon on your home screen and tap it — the app opens full-screen from there, every day.

        On Android — Chrome

        1. Open this page in Chrome.
        2. Tap the ⋮ menu in the top corner.
        3. Tap “Install app” or “Add to Home screen.”
        4. Tap Install / Add to confirm — the gold-path icon lands on your home screen.

        Good to know

        Installing this way is free and needs no App Store account and no password. It is the same app, with the same icon, ready each morning for your counter, reflection, and journal. The App Store version is a separate, later step — this home-screen app works today.
